hero.context: I code with agents extensively. I frame their work with specifications, project context, reusable skills, tests, and reviews. Architecture, shipped code, and the final outcome remain my responsibility.

summary.title: End-to-end product work while staying close to the code
facts: I have spent nearly six years building products at startups and scale-ups, from data modelling and backend work through to interfaces and production.
I am responsible for Webel's web department. At AuroraJobs I led product development within a four-person tech team and built its full-stack Rails application.
I use agents every day to implement more and ship more often. I provide context and constraints, then review the code, tests, and architecture decisions.

selectedWork.title: Technical ownership of products in production
selectedWork.intro: Webel shows how I maintain and evolve several connected applications. AuroraJobs shows how I built and led development of a full-stack product.

items.title: Define the problem
items.description: I establish who it is for, what must change, and what stays out of scope. If the request still bundles several decisions together, I stop before writing code.

items.title: Write the specification
items.description: I document scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria. The implementation is split into parts I can test and review independently.

items.title: Provide context and rules
items.description: The agent gets the existing architecture, repository conventions, design-system documentation, and reusable skills. Those decisions do not need to be reconstructed for every task.

items.title: Implement within boundaries
items.description: Work moves through small changes. If a product decision appears, a constraint breaks, or the approach drifts, I stop the agent, correct the context, and narrow the task again.

items.title: Test and review
items.description: I run automated checks and review the diff, architecture, and browser output. The agent helps with implementation; I decide what ships.

artifacts.title: Scope
artifacts.excerpt: Change the existing flow without duplicating state or altering public routes.

artifacts.title: Behaviour
artifacts.excerpt: The case works in both languages, by keyboard, and without links to pending resources.

artifacts.title: Reusable rule
artifacts.excerpt: Keep the repository conventions and check every output against the specification.

artifacts.title: Before shipping
artifacts.excerpt: Types, tests, responsive layout, accessibility, links, metadata, and visual review.

artifacts.title: Commands
artifacts.excerpt: npm run check-assets && npm run build

items.q: Do I need to know about tech?
items.a: No. Explain it to me the way you would to someone starting at your business, and I'll handle the rest.
It depends on the job. You get a fixed price in writing before I start.
A simple automation takes weeks. An app takes a bit longer. The timeline is in the proposal.
Message me and I'll look at it. If you want it covered at all times, there's a monthly maintenance plan.

items.q: Can I keep using the tools I already have?
items.a: Almost always. If you need something new, I'll explain why before changing anything.

items.q: Do you work with businesses outside Madrid?
items.a: Yes. Almost everything can be done over video call.
